title: Holding on to Grudges
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article examines how grudges, sustained resentment following a serious offense, damage more than the two people directly involved, spilling over into everyone connected to the relationship. It describes how bystanders feel pressured to take sides, become awkward around both parties, and sometimes face requests to withhold kindness from the person out of favor. Quoting the line that "anger is an acid that can do more harm to the vessel in which it is stored," the piece argues resentment mainly damages the person holding it and those around them, not the original offender. The prescribed remedy reframes forgiveness not as forgetting the past but as refusing to let it control the present, which the author says is often persuasive enough to loosen a grudge-holder's grip.
points: Grudges rarely stay contained to the two people involved; the surrounding social circle absorbs the strain and discomfort as well.
People connected to a grudge often feel pressured to take sides or avoid bringing the two parties together, disrupting normal communication.
The "acid" metaphor frames sustained resentment as primarily corrosive to the person holding the grudge and their wider circle, not the original offender.
Reframing forgiveness as "choosing to not let the past affect your present", rather than forgetting, is presented as the argument most likely to loosen a grudge.
quotes: Harboring this bitterness or resentment over time constitutes a grudge.
Unfortunately, the negative feelings underlying a grudge don’t stay contained within the primary relationship.

The spillover effect is that the people surrounding the relationship feel awkward when in the presence of both parties and often have feelings of disloyalty when they support one party more than the other.
Thus, the wisdom in this old saying: “Anger is an acid that can do more harm to the vessel in which it is stored than to anything on which it is poured.
The critical argument to make is this: Forgiveness isn’t about forgetting the past but choosing to not let it affect your present.
